title: Why your basketball film isn't telling you anything
centralQuestion: Why does recorded basketball footage so rarely become useful basketball information?
pointOfView: Film is only valuable when a coach can return to the moments that mattered without rewatching the whole session. Capture quality decides how much of that is possible, and it is decided before any analysis runs.

hooks.chosen: YOUR CAMERA ROLL ISN'T A FILM LAB.
alternates: YOU RECORDED THE WORKOUT. NOW WHO WATCHES IT?
40 MINUTES OF FOOTAGE. FOUR MINUTES THAT MATTER.

claims.claim: Stable, unobstructed film is easier to analyze than shaky or obstructed film
claims.basis: Direct consequence of how the current Axis vision path works: the player box needs a visible, well-lit subject to hold a lock. Stated as a capture principle, not a measured result.

claims.claim: A recorded session has to be rewatched manually before it becomes useful information
claims.basis: True by construction of the status quo the post describes - a raw camera roll file carries no index of its own.
A stated example of a typical gym session length, not a statistic and not a measured Trophy Labs figure.

claims.claim: Trophy Labs holds back when the film cannot support a conclusion
claims.basis: Axis abstention is an active product rule in this repo, not a roadmap promise.
